artworks.title: Danaus Showing the Argives Painted Figurines of Egyptian Gods
artworks.description: Hiltensperger's ceiling panel for the Hermitage's Gallery of the History of Ancient Painting shows Danaus presenting painted Egyptian god-figurines to the Argives — the refugee king as culture-bearer from Egypt to Argos. The scene answers Pausanias' notice that Danaus dedicated the first wooden images at Apollo Lykeios; here the father of the Danaids appears in his own right, not only through his daughters' crime.

artworks.title: Amymone with Her Father (Danaus) and One of Her Sisters
artworks.description: On this Attic red-figure neck amphora (BnF Cabinet des Médailles, De Ridder 359), a hydria-bearing woman runs toward a bearded man with a staff — conventionally read as Amymone (or a sister) approaching Danaus. The Providence Painter gives the Argive father a rare vase presence beside the Danaid he will later arm for the wedding night.

artworks.title: The Daughters of Danaus
artworks.description: Sabatté's wide frieze names Danaus in the title while staging the fifty daughters at their endless labour — the leaking vessel that punishes the crime he commanded. Fin-de-siècle academic painting carries his reception through the Danaids: the father's order made visible as their eternal task.

artworks.title: The Danaides
artworks.description: Waterhouse's Pre-Raphaelite canvas gathers Danaus' daughters around a great vessel, pouring water that will never fill — the underworld sentence for the wedding-night murders he ordered. Private collection; the image became the modern West's default picture of the Danaid myth and, through them, of Danaus' deadly command.

artworks.title: The Danaides Killing Their Husbands
artworks.description: In BnF Français 874 (fol. 170v), the Danaids strike down the sleeping sons of Aegyptus — the massacre Danaus planned after feigning consent to the marriages. The medieval miniature keeps the father's strategy on the page: fifty knives, one wedding night, and the Argive throne secured in blood.

music.title: Les Danaïdes
music.description: Salieri's opera turns Danaus' flight and the wedding-night murders into Enlightenment tragedy — the fifty daughters, the fifty cousins, and the father's command.

popCulture.title: The Suppliants
popCulture.creator: Aeschylus
popCulture.description: Aeschylus brings Danaus and his daughters to Argos as refugees — the father who flees Aegyptus' sons and asks Pelasgus for asylum under Zeus of the suppliant.

popCulture.title: Danaïdes
popCulture.description: Danaus' daughters became a byword: the Danaids who kill their bridegrooms and, in the underworld, fill leaking jars forever — his name carried by their punishment.
